description: WrAFT is a deployable, modular LLM-powered automated writing evaluation and feedback system developed by Adnan Labib and colleagues for argumentative-essay writers.
title: WrAFT (Writing Assessment and Feedback Tool)

description: The Wraparound program is a structured supplemental academic-services programme run by its provider to support academic achievement in a low student-to-teacher-ratio setting.
title: Wraparound program

description: A professional learning programme developed and iteratively tested by the Southwest English Learner Literacy (SWELL) Partnership to improve literacy instruction, support English learners, and incorporate culturally and linguistically relevant instruction.
title: Write to Succeed

description: A computer-based formative-assessment simulation developed by Shah Jatin et al.
title: WriteSim TCExam

description: A 26-item, five-point Likert self-report assessment developed by Daly and Miller to measure writing apprehension and adapted for Turkish learners by Zorbaz.
title: Writing Apprehension Test (Daly & Miller, 1975; Turkish adaptation)

description: Writing Pal is an intelligent tutoring system developed to teach persuasive-writing strategies through explicit instruction, game-based practice, and automated writing evaluation for college-aged learners and students preparing for standardized writing assessments.
title: Writing Pal

description: Writing to Read is a computer-supported beginning-literacy programme developed by IBM that progresses from sound-and-letter production to writing words, sentences, and stories, with supplementary practice activities and progress reporting.
title: Writing to Read

description: A web-based conversational tutoring system developed by Wambsganss et al.
title: WritingTutor

description: A researcher-developed written English-grammar assessment by Jakub Bielak comprising receptive binary-choice and productive constrained constructed-response tasks, administered in parallel split-block versions to Polish senior high school learners.
title: Written discrete-item grammar test of mostly explicit knowledge with three components and split-block test versions
